$comment: The five events the measurement layer records. Kept aggregate-by-day so no event can be joined to a person, which is also what the Associates sub-tag rule requires (SRC-05).

transport.click_redirect: GET /c/<linkId> (302 to the tagged Amazon URL, counted on the way out)
transport.payload: 1x1 no-store response; body is {e, p, l, t} where t is a day key, not a timestamp
transport.identity: no cookie, no localStorage id, no IP retained, no user-agent string stored
transport.sampling: none; the volume this site expects is trivial

events.name: page_view
events.fires: once per document, after the disclosure strip has painted
events.informs: which guide earns arrival; decides the next topic alongside Search Console queries

events.name: product_card_impression
events.fires: when a product card is at least half visible for one second
events.informs: whether the reader scrolls to the shelf at all — separates a copy problem from a placement problem

events.name: outbound_click
events.fires: on any Amazon link, captured before navigation so the count does not race the unload
events.informs: click-through rate by slot; the only honest input to deciding where the buy button belongs. Never carries a per-user identifier.

events.name: gate_block
events.fires: when a reader clicks a product control that the compliance gate has locked
events.informs: how much demand the verification backlog is actually costing — the number that justifies clearing FLG-001 first

events.name: newsletter_signup
events.fires: on submit of the reader-capture form, only when data/forms.json enabled=true
events.informs: whether a reader wants a second email; carries no address, which stays only in the chosen processor
